o.text: Borrowed from German Zink, probably via Russian цинк (cink).
From Proto-Turkic *yara (“wound”), from which Azerbaijani yarıq with the same meaning is also derived.

Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish اورتمك (örtmek), from Proto-Turkic *ört- (“to cover”), whence also Azerbaijani örpək (“headscarf”).
Cognate with Turkish örtmek (“to cover, shut”), Chuvash витме (vitme, “to cover, protect, close”), etc.
Ultimately from Middle Mongol 札撒兀勒 (zhásāwùlè /⁠⁠ǰasa'ul⁠/). Cognate with Mongolian засуул (zasuul).
